title: (No AI) Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
author: Emma Roth
content:
![A photo of Jensen Huang](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/gettyimages-2299645290.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.

At the center of this theory is the [reporting from _The_ _New York Times_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/technology/alice-huang-megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang.html) that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. [US agencies haven't confirmed](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-justice-department-has-not-concluded-alice-huang-was-chinese-spy-blanche-says-2026-11-12/) whether this is the case, and [President Donald Trump claims he was unaware](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1030446/trump-jensen-huang-press-conference) of any spy …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1035027/tech-leaders-nvidia-jensen-huang-theories)

title: (No AI) California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
author: Emma Roth
content:
![An illustration of the OpenAI logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/10/STK155_OPEN_AI_4_CVirginia_D.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In [a lawsuit filed Monday](https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28912394-california-v-openai/), Attorney General [Rob Bonta accuses](https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/it%E2%80%99s-golden-state-not-wild-west-attorney-general-bonta-sues-openai-over) OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," [as reported earlier by _Reuters_](https://www.reuters.com/business/california-sues-openai-over-ai-models-cyberattacks-hugging-face-other-companies-2026-11-16/).

The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general's office that it "lost control" of its AI agents …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1034815/california-openai-hugging-face-lawsuit)
